key_insight: Quantum simulations designed to calculate response functions also prepare many-body states that reveal how information propagates, becomes accessible, and supports entanglement.
engineering_relevance: Existing response-simulation protocols could be reused to study information readout and quantum communication without designing an entirely new state-preparation protocol.
method: Study local-pulse Green-function protocols in finite XX and XXX spin chains.
Encode a classical bit through opposite source rotations and track its distribution and measurement accessibility.
Analyze reduced states for source-angle estimation, Bell-state recovery, communication rates, and entanglement.
evidence_signal: In the studied chains, fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed XX response, yet simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of locally available information in XXX; this ordering also holds for local source-angle estimation.
watch_item: The case study uses finite XX and XXX chains, so generalization to other models and noisy hardware remains to be established.
paper_title: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
